Text S1 ESI FT-ICR MS analysis

PPL /C18-Solid phase extraction procedure. All DOM samples were desalted by an established SPE procedure using Agilent Bond Elut-PPL cartridges (500 mg per 6 mL). Specifically, samples were first acidified by hydrochloric acid (HCl, 1 mol/L) to pH 2.0 to improve the recovery of phenolic and carboxylic substances [1]. Notably, the solution was diluted to ~2–3 mg-(dissolved organic carbon (DOC))/L to avoid protein precipitation in DOM [2, 3]. The acidified samples were pumped at ~2 mL/min through the cartridges, which had been pre-activated with 12 mL methanol (LC-MS grade) and 12mL acidified ultrapure water (pH 2.0).Next, the cartridges were rinsed with 18 mL acidified ultrapure water to remove the residual salts, dried with a stream of N2, and immediately eluted by 12 mL methanol to recover DOM. The eluted samples were blow-dried with N2 and the eluate was stored at -20 ℃ after freeze-drying. Before FT-ICR MS analysis, the dried eluate was solubilized by 1:1 methanol/water (v/v) solution. After the sample testing was completed, the internal standard calibration was then performed using small molecule standards. The resulting data were assigned an in-house MATLAB algorithm named NOMDBP created by Fu et al.[4].The performance criteria for automatic molecular formula matching were set as follows: the relative error between the measured value and the matching value for any mass-to-charge ratio was less than 1 ppm, and the peak height signal-to-noise ratio S/N was ≥ 4.
Text S2 Van Krevelen diagrams boundary regions

Dividing the Van Krevelen diagram into regions corresponding to seven compound classes based on of O/C and H/C ratios. The stoichiometric ranges used to establish the classification boundaries follow: lipids for H/C = 1.5-2.0, O/C = 0-0.3; aliphatic/proteins for H/C = 1.5-2.2, O/C = 0.3-0.67; lignin/CRAM-like for H/C = 0.7-1.5, O/C = 0.1-0.67; carbohydrates for H/C = 1.5-2.4, O/C = 0.67-1.2; unsaturated hydrocarbons for H/C = 0.7-1.5, O/C = 0-0.1; aromatic structures for H/C = 0.2-0.7, O/C = 0-0.67; and tannin for H/C = 0.6-1.5, O/C = 0.67-1.0 [5].
Text S3 Calculation of molecular parameters

After obtaining the molecular formulas of DOM in the digested sludge, it can be classified into organic compounds of CHO, CHON, CHOS, and CHONS types according to the stoichiometric number of molecular elements. Molecular parameters such as H/C, O/C, DBE, Xc, NOSC, and AImod were then calculated based on the atomic numbers of C, H, O, and N in the molecular formulas. The magnitude-averaged Cw, Hw, Ow, Nw, O/Cw, H/Cw, DBEw, NOSCw and AImodw values were used to estimate the averaged molecular characteristics of DOM, where the value of the peak intensity was the average of all the test results [6-8].

where C, H, O and N represent the number of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen atoms per molecular formula, respectively; M represents parameters of C, H, O, N, O/C, H/C, DBE, NOSC and AImod, respectively; w signifies a magnitude-weighted calculation, and Ii and Mi are the peak intensity and M value of peak i, respectively.
